rules.title: Ban on AI apartment rent-pricing software
rules.requirement: Santa Ana apartment owners and landlords may not use automated AI or algorithmic software to set rental prices. The ordinance is intended to stop artificially inflated rental rates and unfair rent increases from Algorithmic Devices.

coverage.summary: Applies to Santa Ana apartment owners and landlords; the article does not state building age, size, or tenancy-type limits.

rules.penalty: Landlords caught using the banned software could be fined $1,000.
rules.interaction: The article notes similar city bans in San Francisco, San Diego, and Berkeley and quotes an industry representative referring to recently adopted California state regulations, but it does not state any preemption or hierarchy.
rules.quoted_span: “The purpose and intent of this [ordinance] is to protect the residents of Santa Ana from artificially inflated rental rates and unfair rent increases by prohibiting the sale, licensing and use of Algorithmic Devices,” according to a staff report.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-pricing software
rules.requirement: San Francisco has banned similar rent-pricing software that uses algorithms to analyze private competitor data to set monthly rents. The article does not state the ordinance’s exact operative terms.

coverage.summary: Coverage details are not stated beyond a city ban on similar algorithmic rent-pricing software.

rules.interaction: The article cites this as an existing city ban similar to Santa Ana’s ordinance, without stating how it interacts with state or other local law.
rules.quoted_span: Cities like San Francisco, San Diego and Berkeley have already banned similar software that uses algorithms to analyze private competitor data to set monthly rents.
